skill.name: scientific-critical-thinking
skill.description: Evaluate scientific claims, research methods, experimental design, statistics, bias, confounding, and evidence quality with structured critical-thinking frameworks.
skill.summary: Assess research rigor using methodology, bias, statistics, evidence hierarchy, GRADE, and logical fallacy checks.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown prose, reference paths, and checklist terms. The remaining risks are a Bash-enabled schematic workflow and broad Write, Edit, and Bash permissions for a research review skill. No prompt injection text or explicit data-exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Bash and file-write permissions are broader than core review needs
remediation.suggestion: Remove Bash, Write, and Edit from allowed-tools unless the skill must create files. If retained, require explicit user confirmation before commands or file writes.

remediation.issue: Local schematic command can execute project code
remediation.suggestion: Make the Python command optional, document the trusted script path, and require confirmation before running it with manuscript-derived inputs.

remediation.issue: External schematic workflow may process sensitive research content
remediation.suggestion: State whether scientific-schematics or Nano Banana Pro sends content to external services, and require approval before sharing unpublished work.

content.value_statement: Scientific claims are hard to assess because methods, statistics, and bias risks can be hidden. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured evidence review.
actual_capabilities: Reviews study design, validity, controls, measurement quality, and causal claims.
Identifies bias risks including confirmation bias, selection bias, attrition, publication bias, and p-hacking.
Evaluates statistical reporting, p-values, confidence intervals, power, effect sizes, and model assumptions.
Applies evidence quality concepts including GRADE, Cochrane risk of bias, and study hierarchy.
Uses included references for scientific method, experimental design, logical fallacies, bias, and statistical pitfalls.
Suggests more precise claims, hedging language, and methodological improvements.
limitations: It does not perform automated literature searches or retrieve current papers by itself.
It does not replace peer review, statistical consulting, or domain expert judgment.
It cannot verify raw data integrity unless the user provides data and methods.
Diagram generation depends on a separate schematic skill or a trusted local script.

use_cases.title: Review a Manuscript Draft
use_cases.description: Check methods, statistics, limitations, and claim strength before submission.

use_cases.title: Assess Evidence for Decisions
use_cases.description: Compare study quality, bias risks, and certainty before using evidence in guidance.

use_cases.title: Improve Science Communication
use_cases.description: Identify overstated claims, logical fallacies, and missing context in articles or summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Claim Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this scientific claim for evidence strength, bias risks, and overstatement. Claim: [paste claim].

prompt_templates.title: Paper Methods Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this paper excerpt. Assess study design, sampling, controls, measurements, statistics, and limits on causal inference.

prompt_templates.title: Evidence Quality Comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these studies using evidence hierarchy and GRADE concepts. Identify consistency, bias, indirectness, imprecision, and publication bias.

prompt_templates.title: Study Design Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this proposed study protocol. Check hypotheses, variables, randomization, blinding, sample size, analysis plan, ethics, and reporting standards.

output_examples.input: A news article says a supplement prevents dementia because supplement users had lower dementia rates in an observational study.
output_examples.output: The causal claim is stronger than the study design supports. Key concerns are confounding, selection bias, and healthy-user effects. A safer conclusion is that the supplement is associated with lower observed rates, pending stronger evidence.

output_examples.input: A trial reports p = 0.04 for one of twenty exploratory outcomes and presents it as the main finding.
output_examples.output: The result needs caution. Multiple testing raises false-positive risk, and exploratory outcomes should be labeled clearly. Report adjusted analyses, effect sizes, and confidence intervals.

output_examples.input: A proposal plans to test a behavioral intervention without blinding or a prespecified analysis plan.
output_examples.output: Main risks are performance bias, detection bias, and analysis flexibility. Use blinded outcome assessment when possible, preregister the analysis, and define primary outcomes before data collection.

best_practices: Provide the study question, design, sample, outcomes, and statistical methods with the prompt.
Ask for separate sections on strengths, limitations, bias risks, and conclusion support.
Use the detailed reference files when the review needs formal criteria or checklists.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a verdict without providing methods, measures, and outcome details.
Do not treat evidence hierarchy as a substitute for study quality assessment.
Do not use the skill to manufacture certainty when evidence is weak or indirect.

faq.question: Does this skill search for new papers?
faq.answer: No. It evaluates material you provide and references included frameworks. Use separate browsing or database tools for current literature.

faq.question: Can it grade evidence with GRADE?
faq.answer: It can apply GRADE concepts when enough study details are available, but final certainty ratings need expert review.

faq.question: Can it detect statistical errors?
faq.answer: It can flag common issues such as underpowering, p-hacking, multiple testing, weak effect reporting, and assumption violations.

faq.question: Is it suitable for medical decisions?
faq.answer: It can support evidence review, but it is not medical advice and does not replace qualified clinical judgment.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Methods sections, protocols, abstracts, claims, tables, study summaries, and notes about sample, design, outcomes, and analyses work best.

faq.question: Does it generate diagrams?
faq.answer: It can suggest diagrams. Actual schematic generation depends on an optional external skill or trusted local script.
